name: Kshama for Congress
subject: Solidarity with Chris Smalls!
body:
We need a new party if we want to defeat the billionaires and end the wars.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/kshamasawant/socialists-for-kshama-13701873?e=bbdb764b3a)
---
| | | | | |

Dear Peter,
Jacobin magazine, the principal publication associated with the leadership of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), yesterday released a [hit piece](https://us.list-manage.com/fMOiMJxid96?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) on Amazon labor leader Chris Smalls.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/gMJ28wCD5aD?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15)
| | Photo Credit - [Legoktm](https://us.list-manage.com/26O4iFGVEAg?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15)
---
| | Brother Smalls was one of the main leaders of the Amazon Labor Union (ALU), which won the first-ever union in an Amazon warehouse in the United States, at the JFK8 warehouse on Staten Island, in 2022. Smalls has also been a prominent activist fighting against the genocide in Gaza and in solidarity with the Palestinian people.
Jacobin’s article is a hatchet job against a leading labor activist who has refused to toe the line of the DSA and the business unionist labor leaders. They have turned on Smalls as they will turn on anyone who gets in the way of their efforts to give cover to the so-called progressive Democrats and to the Democratic Party as a whole, which they do despite endless betrayals by Democrats against working people.
**The crux of the real reason why Jacobin went after Smalls is contained in this sentence: “[Smalls] blames the two-party system for the state of the American labor movement...”**
Smalls is spot on about this and the need to break from the Democratic and Republican parties. **We urgently need a new party of the working class.**
**The DSA leadership, on the other hand, sees giving cover to the Democratic Party as job number one.** The Democratic Party is the party under whom the genocide in Gaza began, with Democrat Joe Biden in the White House. The overwhelming majority of Congressional Democrats voted to fund Israel’s genocide as well as to block U.N. food aid to Gaza, including 56 members of the so-called Cogressional Progressive Caucus. Biden and the Democrats also engineered the breaking of the railroad workers’ strike. ALL Democrats in the House, including DSA star AOC voted to break the strike.
The Democratic Party is not a “lesser evil”, but one of the two most powerful capitalist parties in the world, and in no way represents working people or the oppressed.
---
|
---
| | **SUPPORT MY INDEPENDENT SOCIALIST****CAMPAIGN FOR CONGRESS!**
[**Join me Sunday, June 7th at 4pm PT / 7pm ET**](https://us.list-manage.com/oCu5ma5qeOk?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15)**Town Hall: Stop the Data Centers and AI Layoffs!**
[**Get all the info and RSVP on the event page!**](https://us.list-manage.com/zy0tx0w2wnT?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15)
---
| [DONATE TODAY](https://us.list-manage.com/q4AdNWvRZXM?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15)
---
| [VOLUNTEER](https://us.list-manage.com/f5IVk6sBjVP?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15)
---
| | Business unionist labor leaders are those who have made peace with the capitalist system and the bosses and oppose any kind of class struggle methods. They are driven by protecting their careers, which means placating the bosses and their political servants, not organizing the rank and file against the bosses to win substantive working-class victories. Refusing to fight the bosses also means not only aligning with, but being in lockstep with the parties of the bosses, like the Democratic Party.
The overwhelming majority of the labor leadership today is business unionist, with some crucial exceptions like Smalls. This also means that they are mostly aligned with the Democratic Party, with a few prominent figures like Teamster President Sean O’Brien shamefully making public overtures to Trump and the Republicans.
Jacobin and the DSA leadership had no critique of UAW President Shawn Fain when he [loudly championed](https://us.list-manage.com/DZvutgvKtGw?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) Kamala Harris for President at the Chicago Democratic National Convention in 2024. Fain declared in his speech that Harris had “stood shoulder to shoulder with the working class,” that she “is one of us,” and “she's a fighter for the working class.”
Straightforward facts and Jacobin’s own analysis prove Fain’s remarks to be gravely false and misleading. Harris was the Vice President in an administration that presided over the funding of the genocide in Gaza and the breaking of the railroad workers’ strike. On top of that, by Jacobin’s own admission, Harris ran a Presidential election campaign in which she completely [refused](https://us.list-manage.com/ntbnryg7SuE?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) to make any concession to any of the many “wildly popular” working-class demands such as Medicare for All or universal, paid family leave. Jacobin also [reported](https://us.list-manage.com/ZKOLrerEGIX?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) that as a District Attorney in California, Harris targeted working-class and poor people, prosecuting “cases of elementary school truancy and marijuana, opposing its legalization. Cannabis arrests increased through most of her time in office, along with the percentage of black cannabis arrestees. The conviction rate for those offenses increased, too.”
It wasn’t just Fain, of course. Virtually the entire labor leadership uncritically cheered Harris on despite her refusal to express support of even minimal demands like a national $15/hour minimum wage, let alone publicly come out against the genocide in Gaza. The DNC’s own autopsy of the Harris loss reveals that the party’s contempt for the majority of working people angry about the genocide and the cost-of-living crisis cost them the election.
I am running as a pro-worker antiwar socialist against Adam Smith, a 29-year warmongering incumbent Democrat who has voted for tens of billions of dollars for the genocide in Gaza, to slash hundreds of billions of dollars from Medicare and Medicaid, to create and fund ICE, to break the railroad workers’ strike, and to bail out the super-rich after the 2008 Great Recession.
Yet, the leadership of the [Washington State Labor Council](https://us.list-manage.com/Ofrp4XpWQ4h?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) and the [Washington Education Association](https://us.list-manage.com/qndwsnH_zjR?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) recently endorsed Adam Smith, without even inviting our campaign to speak to their membership.
The labor leadership’s refusal to break from the genocidal parties of the capitalist bosses, and their eagerness to actively promote them, is one of the biggest obstacles to any victories for the antiwar movement or the working class. We need a reckoning in the labor movement.
The article on Smalls is purportedly to critique him for not focusing on the battle to win a contract at JFK8 after the historic union election, instead “traveling the country, ostensibly to help other Amazon warehouses unionize.” There are legitimate and necessary debates to be had about strategy and tactics. But furnishing this as the excuse for a vitriolic hit piece is completely disingenuous. For this reason, the article has earned a public and resounding rebuke from working people and union members.
In fact, the 2022 ALU union election campaign at JFK8 was a departure from the business unionist strategy we’ve seen over the past several decades under much of the labor leadership. The campaign was organized around a set of clear and material demands. Thirty dollars an hour starting pay for tier 1 workers, real paid time off, longer breaks, an end to broad mandatory overtime. These demands were not picked out of thin air. They were born out of conversations among co-workers on the shop floor, in the break rooms, and on the bus. The demands were at the front and center of the campaign and relentlessly brought up in speeches and plastered on campaign leaflets, not merely listed on the union website somewhere. The campaign based itself on tireless shop-floor organizing and mobilizing rank-and-file workers. The campaign leaders made clear to their fellow workers from day one that the fight for a union would put them in direct conflict with Amazon executives. That there would be no peaceful partnership between the workers and executives, that the interests of the bosses are at complete odds with ours. That workers would need to fight in large numbers.
The approach ALU leaders used to win the union election at JFK8 are what I would call class struggle methods. It is no coincidence that this is the only successful union election at an Amazon warehouse in America to date. For instance, attempts by the Retail, Wholesale and Department Store Union (RWDSU) to unionize an Amazon warehouse in Bessemer, Alabama, failed precisely because the union leadership refused to use similar class struggle methods. Instead, they built a campaign that did not mobilize the warehouse workforce in large numbers. The leadership also refused to raise concrete demands, and instead put forward vague sentiments like "respect at work." All of this meant that the union drive was twice crushed by the vicious union busting by Amazon bosses.
The refusal to build union campaigns around concrete and bold demands that can ignite a fire among the rank and file to activate them as an organized force is a common mistake by business unionist leaders. It is a mistake, however, that flows from their desire not to antagonize the bosses. Class struggle unionist leaders understand that a campaign to unionize a workplace or for a union to fight for a decent contract WILL antagonize the bosses. The only way to win is to embrace a militant fightback, which requires leaders who are not looking to make their own personal careers.
Unionizing a behemoth like Amazon will require organizing on a scale proportionate to the task of taking on the might of the billionaire class. It will need a strategy that launches unionizing drives simultaneously at multiple warehouses, with strike preparations on a colossal scale. Further union victories, much less a winning union contract, are only possible at Amazon on the basis of an all-out militant fightback like the one led by revolutionary socialists in the 1934 Minneapolis General Strike and the subsequent, militant sit-down strikes that unionized the auto industry. It’s ironic for Jacobin to single out Smalls because unionizing Amazon will need precisely the class struggle unionism that has been missing in the labor leadership that Jacobin has defended, or given cover to, for years.
Class struggle unionist leaders understand that what workers can win will come only from a determined, organized, and relentless fightback against the bosses. Class struggle unionists fight to prevent scab workers from being able to break the strike by organizing community-wide working-class solidarity campaigns. They urge members of other unions to stand with the strike and also carry out solidarity strikes. Crucially, class struggle unionist leaders also recognize that the political parties of capitalism represent the capitalist state and exist to defend the interests of the capitalist class. In the United States, that means understanding that both the Democratic and Republican parties are hostile to the interests of workers. It means having a strategy to defeat the repression and even violence that the Democrats and Republicans will use, and have historically used again and again, in order to break strikes.
Class struggle unionism means recognizing that the actual purpose of “progressives” in the Democratic Party is to try to whitewash the party’s pro-capitalist agenda. New York City hospital bosses spent upwards of $100 million in hiring out-of-state scab nurses in an attempt to undercut the historic strike of nurses at the start of this year. New York’s Democratic Governor Kathy Hochul signed, and repeatedly renewed, an executive order making it easier for the bosses to hire the scabs. NYC’s Democratic Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who is a prominent DSA leader, visited the picket line of the nurses but also shamefully endorsed Hochul for her re-election bid _during_ the strike.
Brother Smalls has put his life on the line for the antiwar movement in solidarity with the Palestinian people against the Israeli state’s genocide bankrolled by both the Democratic and Republican parties. Smalls went on a Gaza aid flotilla carrying food, baby formula, diapers, and medicine in the context of catastrophic levels of mass starvation in Gaza. The flotilla was attacked by the Israeli military, who physically assaulted Smalls, and kicked and choked him.
In contrast, AOC has voted for the Iron Dome which is a key part of the Israeli state’s genocidal apparatus. At the 2024 Democratic National Convention, AOC blatantly lied, saying Democratic candidate Kamala Harris was working tirelessly to secure a ceasefire in Gaza.
Jacobin and much of the DSA leadership have regularly [shielded AOC](https://us.list-manage.com/qTjw5OC9NO_?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) from the legitimate anger at her betrayals of working people and the antiwar movement. Shamefully, AOC still has the endorsement of New York City DSA. In the article, Jacobin accuses Smalls of using his platform “to lash out at labor’s allies,” clearly referring to his criticisms of AOC and other “progressive” Democrats.
**Because Smalls has the temerity to expose AOC and other self-described “progressive” politicians, Jacobin calls him “narcissistic.”** The magazine’s editors were apparently forced to retract this term, changing their article title, after they got huge amounts of flak on all social media for their article on Smalls.
Personal attacks and character assassination like in this case are often used by the political establishment’s spokespeople as a proxy for their real objection: any leader openly calling out the actual role of the so-called progressive Democrats and of the Democratic Party as a whole.
There is huge anger among the American working class at both the Democratic and Republican parties. Any idea that the Democratic Party is a friend of working people has been disproven a thousand times over. Working people aren’t being fooled.
Poll after poll has shown that tens of millions of working and young people are furious at the wars, the cost-of-living crisis, and at both parties of the billionaires. A [New York Times/Siena poll](https://us.list-manage.com/10J99F2FyZY?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15) released last month shows that “political disillusionment seems only to be deepening.” The survey estimates that only 26 percent of voters are happy with the Democratic Party and only 33 percent with the Republican Party. **Nearly two-thirds of respondents under the age of 30 are angry with both parties.**
Yet, Democrats and Republicans keep getting re-elected. Democrats and Republicans, led by my main opponent, Democrat Adam Smith, just put forward a bill for a trillion new dollars for war. Working people are still struggling to get their most basic needs met.
**How does one explain the chasm between what most of us working people want and what we end up getting?** It is the lack of virtually any principled leaders who unambiguously fight for working people and pose a direct challenge to the Democratic Party and the billionaires and multimillionaires they represent.
A big reason it is extremely difficult to build this type of independent leadership is that working people immediately come up against gatekeepers the moment they try to fight for their interests.
**Who are the gatekeepers?** They are individuals who pose as being on the side of working people but whose actual role is to block working-class movements and to defend the political establishment and the billionaires they represent. Business unionist leaders themselves and the so-called progressive Democrats they give cover to are both playing the role of gatekeepers. Their main goal is to give an illusion of debate with Trump and the Republicans in order to keep working people straitjacketed inside the two parties of capitalism.
I have seen gatekeepers in action first hand over and over during my decade as the sole socialist on the Seattle City Council. My office won the nation’s highest minimum wage, the Amazon Tax, free abortion in Seattle, unprecedented renters’ rights, and much more. But I was only able to win these because I used my office and built mass movements, despite the opposition from the gatekeepers, including business unionists, NGO leaders, and progressive Democrats.
Overcoming gatekeepers is also the only avenue of rebuilding a militant labor movement and actually defeating the billionaires and multimillionaires. That avenue means we need to pose a concrete threat to both the Democratic and Republican parties, which in turn requires a challenge to the business unionist labor leadership. In other words, the tasks of overcoming the gatekeepers and defeating capitalism’s two parties are inseparable.
That is why I am now running as an independent revolutionary socialist against genocidal Democrat Adam Smith, because we desperately need principled and relentless fighters in Congress. I am the only candidate in this race calling for an end to all military aid to Israel and an end to all weapons and tech for genocide and imperialist war.
I’m the only candidate prepared to go to class war against the billionaires and their two parties.

In solidarity,
Kshama Sawant

**We did it!** Thanks to the hard work of volunteers and supporters across Wisconsin's 5th Congressional District, we successfully submitted our nomination signatures to the Wisconsin Elections Commission. That means **Beck for Congress will officially be on the ballot this November against Republican Scott Fitzgerald.** Even better, there is **no Democratic primary** , so we are heading straight into the General Election. I want to personally thank everyone who collected signatures, circulated nomination papers, attended events, talked to friends and neighbors, and helped make this milestone possible. This campaign would not exist without you. Now the real work begins. Our campaign is transitioning into **full General Election mode** , and we need your help more than ever. **Scott Fitzgerald** has the advantages of incumbency, party infrastructure, and big-money donors. What we have is something more powerful: **people**. This campaign is a true grassroots effort, and it will take all of us working together to build a common front against the Republican machine and bring change to Wisconsin's 5th Congressional District. Here's how you can help right now:
* Volunteer with the campaign.
* Put a Beck for Congress yard sign in your yard.
* Tell your friends, family, coworkers, and neighbors about our campaign.
* Like, share, comment on, and forward our social media posts.
* Attend campaign events and bring a friend.
* Write letters to the editor.
* Help us spread the word in your community.

I have one simple challenge for every supporter: **Tell 10 people about Beck for Congress and ask each of them to tell 10 more people. Then forward this email to 10 people who care about the future of our district and our democracy.** That's how grassroots movements grow. That's how we build name recognition. That's how we compete with big money. And that's how we win. As I continue to sound like a broken record, our campaign runs on **small-dollar donations from people like you.** We don't have corporate PAC money or wealthy special interests funding our campaign. We are powered by neighbors, friends, working families, retirees, students, and people who believe Wisconsin deserves better representation in Congress. [Donate Here!](https://v8k6.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=6a249406efacc76ce94f01d0&u=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fbeck-for-congress-1&w=65ec894f1812f45661bb4481&c=b_69ef97b6d824417cd99d8016&l=en-US&s=RSRP4Dy8-g2OQHKXGgAXijUihGo%3D) If you can, please make a contribution today. Then ask a friend to do the same. Every donation helps us print literature, purchase yard signs, attend community events, communicate with voters, and build the campaign operation needed to defeat **Scott Fitzgerald** in November. The road ahead won't be easy, but together we can offer voters a real choice and a new direction for Wisconsin's 5th Congressional District. **A change will do you good.** Thank you for your support, your energy, and your belief in this campaign. Thanks to the hard work of volunteers and supporters across Wisconsin's 5th Congressional District, we successfully submitted our nomination signatures to the Wisconsin Elections Commission | | | | | We did it! Thanks to the hard work of volunteers and supporters across Wisconsin's 5th Congressional District, we successfully submitted our nomination signatures to the Wisconsin Elections Commission. That means Beck for Congress will officially be on the ballot this November against Republican Scott Fitzgerald. Even better, there is no Democratic primary , so we are heading straight into the General Election. I want to personally thank everyone who collected signatures, circulated nomination papers, attended events, talked to friends and neighbors, and helped make this milestone possible. This campaign would not exist without you. Now the real work begins. Our campaign is transitioning into full General Election mode , and we need your help more than ever. Scott Fitzgerald has the advantages of incumbency, party infrastructure, and big-money donors. What we have is something more powerful: people. This campaign is a true grassroots effort, and it will take all of us working together to build a common front against the Republican machine and bring change to Wisconsin's 5th Congressional District. Here's how you can help right now: Volunteer with the campaign. Put a Beck for Congress yard sign in your yard. Tell your friends, family, coworkers, and neighbors about our campaign. Like, share, comment on, and forward our social media posts. Attend campaign events and bring a friend. Write letters to the editor. Help us spread the word in your community. I have one simple challenge for every supporter: Tell 10 people about Beck for Congress and ask each of them to tell 10 more people. Then forward this email to 10 people who care about the future of our district and our democracy. That's how grassroots movements grow. That's how we build name recognition. That's how we compete with big money. And that's how we win. As I continue to sound like a broken record, our campaign runs on small-dollar donations from people like you. We don't have corporate PAC money or wealthy special interests funding our campaign. We are powered by neighbors, friends, working families, retirees, students, and people who believe Wisconsin deserves better representation in Congress. If you can, please make a contribution today. Then ask a friend to do the same. Every donation helps us print literature, purchase yard signs, attend community events, communicate with voters, and build the campaign operation needed to defeat Scott Fitzgerald in November. The road ahead won't be easy, but together we can offer voters a real choice and a new direction for Wisconsin's 5th Congressional District. A change will do you good.** Thank you for your support, your energy, and your belief in this campaign. Let's get to work. Onward to November, Andy | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|--- Authorized and paid for by: Beck for Congress Beck for Congress, PO Box 235, West Bend, WI 53095, United States

Hello Peter, I'd like to introduce myself.

My name is Jackie Mary Auringer, and I'm running for U.S. Congress because I am no longer willing to leave the future of my community in the hands of people I can't trust.

For too long, the voices of families in the Hudson Valley have been ignored or filtered through agendas, which don't reflect what life is really like here, especially as the cost of living continues to rise and families are stretched thinner every year.

**I am not bought by outside interests, nor am I driven by personal ambition.**

My commitment is simple: independence, integrity, and service to every person in New York's 18th District.

My loyalty is to this community, its families, its future, and its strength.

Our nation is too divided, and it's holding us back.

I believe we can do better.

We can lead with purpose, bring people together, focus on real results, support families, and rebuild confidence in our leadership.

My focus is on advancing practical solutions that support families like mine, bolster local businesses, and strengthen our community as a whole.

clean_body: My commitment is simple: independence, integrity, and service to every person in New York's 18th District. | Hello Peter, I'd like to introduce myself. My name is Jackie Mary Auringer, and I'm running for U.S. Congress because I am no longer willing to leave the future of my community in the hands of people I can't trust. For too long, the voices of families in the Hudson Valley have been ignored or filtered through agendas, which don't reflect what life is really like here, especially as the cost of living continues to rise and families are stretched thinner every year. I am not bought by outside interests, nor am I driven by personal ambition. My commitment is simple: independence, integrity, and service to every person in New York's 18th District. My loyalty is to this community, its families, its future, and its strength. Our nation is too divided, and it's holding us back. I believe we can do better. We can lead with purpose, bring people together, focus on real results, support families, and rebuild confidence in our leadership. My focus is on advancing practical solutions that support families like mine, bolster local businesses, and strengthen our community as a whole. I'm a proud Hudson Valley native. I was born and raised there and shaped by parents who dedicated their lives to serving it, my mother as a teacher and my father through his construction business. They taught me what matters: responsibility, accountability, and pride in where you come from. Growing up in that environment gave me a firsthand understanding of the importance of hard work, community involvement, and local pride. That perspective is what drives my commitment to ensuring the Hudson Valley is represented by someone who knows it, values it, and will always put it first. I believe that family is the foundation. This lens formed my values and the way I approach servant leadership. That means being a good neighbor and respecting others. The Hudson Valley shaped every part of who I am, and I am committed to protecting our way of life to ensure future generations can thrive in our community. Just like my family did. So, I'm humbly asking for your support before my major campaign deadline on June 15th as I embark on this mission to give my hometown the representation it's longed for. I've got your back, Peter. Thank you very much, Jackie Auringer Candidate for Congress NY-18 All The Way With JMA | | Paid for by Jackie Auringer for Congress Don't want to receive any more of our emails? name: Emily Randall for Congress
subject: What we were up to in May:
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Emily Randall for Congress
body:
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132846653/625874478/1231236074?refcode=RS_EM_FR_2026.06.06_MayNewsletterResend&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NzI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmNjVmNDQzOC1mNjYxLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ykw6O7pPuoR80WoBoM0185JLBvUENIqQtY7UN6nX1dw=&emci=6f57180e-b361-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&emdi=f65f4438-f661-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&ceid=23483442) | Hey, Peter. **May was all about one question:** _Why are working families paying more while Republicans in the other Washington keep prioritizing everything except lowering costs?_ **Putting my foot down** — I voted NO on the Republican budget that did absolutely nothing to lower costs for working families. Instead of helping Americans afford groceries, gas, healthcare, or childcare, Republicans proposed billions in new spending for immigration enforcement and other Trump administration priorities. Working people deserve a budget that lowers costs and invests in their future, not one that ignores the challenges they face every day. **Protecting what makes Washington special** — I continued the fight to protect our public lands and preserve the natural beauty of the Olympic Peninsula. As the Trump administration pushed to weaken protections for roadless areas, I spoke out in support of the Roadless Rule and renewed my commitment to passing the Wild Olympics Wilderness & Wild and Scenic Rivers Act. Protecting our forests, rivers, and Tribal ancestral lands is about safeguarding these places for future generations. **Making life more affordable** — Families across our district are feeling squeezed by rising costs and stagnant wages. As Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus Better Pay and Benefits Task Force, I’m working with my colleagues to advance policies that put working people first. Putting my foot down — I voted NO on the Republican budget that did absolutely nothing to lower costs for working families. Instead of helping Americans afford groceries, gas, healthcare, or childcare, Republicans proposed billions in new spending for immigration enforcement and other Trump administration priorities. Working people deserve a budget that lowers costs and invests in their future, not one that ignores the challenges they face every day. Protecting what makes Washington special — I continued the fight to protect our public lands and preserve the natural beauty of the Olympic Peninsula. As the Trump administration pushed to weaken protections for roadless areas, I spoke out in support of the Roadless Rule and renewed my commitment to passing the Wild Olympics Wilderness & Wild and Scenic Rivers Act. Protecting our forests, rivers, and Tribal ancestral lands is about safeguarding these places for future generations. Making life more affordable — Families across our district are feeling squeezed by rising costs and stagnant wages. As Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus Better Pay and Benefits Task Force, I’m working with my colleagues to advance policies that put working people first. From lowering costs to strengthening pay and benefits, we're focused on building an economy that works for everyone. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. | Fellow American,
There is a stark difference between a Maine work ethic and a Washington political stunt.
The Radical Left's poster boy, Graham Platner, has plenty of time to pose for magazine covers and sit for glowing interviews with the New York Times.
Why? Because he simply isn't working.
He claims to be a "working-class oyster farmer," but the reality is far different. For the past decade, Platner has not held a full-time job. He has been passively growing oysters and enjoying a leisurely life, all while Chuck Schumer and Elizabeth Warren prop him up as their handpicked candidate to flip Maine blue. Now, he is bending the truth in glossy photo shoots, trying to convince voters that he will work hard for our state.
Mainers know what real hard work looks like.

# [](https://act.electjon.com/go/4629?t=1&akid=2359%2E5691347%2EV8eg06)

Last weekend, Jon took the stage in Atlanta to talk about what is happening in America.
_From his speech:_
**“The Mar-a-Lago mafia has taken American corruption to spectacular new heights, but corruption in America runs a lot deeper than Donald Trump.** American politics is coin-operated.
Money goes in, favors come out, and that's why spectacular wealth buys an ever-greater share of power over our national affairs, while the mere citizen is treated with contempt.
_Citizens United_ was the most destructive court decision in modern American history. It's unleashed a flood of secret money, corporate money, billionaire money on both sides.”
_But this broken moment is an opening, not for restoration, but for reformation._
Peter, as we head into the midterm elections, we have a chance to change the narrative...
Regaining Congressional control is the only way out of this descent into an un‐American America.
And we can start by reelecting Jon in Georgia.
[**Jon can’t win alone. He needs all of us, working together, to create a grassroots movement ready to take on the wave of attacks coming from the Republicans. Can you give $5, $10, or even $25 to help Jon win in November? Any amount will help.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-jun26.cWQ5pb&refcode=em260606-1-f-l&t=2&akid=2359%2E5691347%2EV8eg06)

Friend, For years, right-wing operatives and billionaire donors have built a political machine designed to weaken voting rights, reshape the courts, and entrench minority rule across the country. Now we are seeing the consequences everywhere. After the Supreme Court weakened protections against racial gerrymandering, Republican legislatures immediately moved to redraw maps that dismantle Black political representation in states like Tennessee, Alabama, and Louisiana.
* Courts are overriding voter-approved reforms.
* Polling protections are being stripped away.
* Election rules are being rewritten in the middle of election cycles.

And behind much of it is an enormous pipeline of dark money funding the legal campaigns, political pressure operations, extremist litigation, and disinformation efforts driving this anti-democracy agenda forward. These networks are not spending millions by accident. They understand something very clearly: **If they can weaken voting rights, manipulate representation, and control who gets political power, they can hold onto power even when voters reject them.** That is the strategy. And while their donors write massive checks behind closed doors, organizations fighting to protect democracy are powered by grassroots people giving what they can because they understand what is at stake. That includes this community. At Voting Rights Fund, we are tracking redistricting fights, supporting rapid-response democracy messaging, exposing attacks on voting rights, and helping build the public pressure needed to fight back before the 2026 elections are reshaped even further. **[But we cannot afford to fall behind while the right’s dark money machine accelerates.](http://links.votingrightsfund.org/s/c/EUQ1ORf5Z9dTX1_8Zynw4yjo-LuH17R9GwX61tgV9fH_TrvT-9BzM9GTdMD3Wez2UGhXCjFOComvfbWNstszDwbNm2Z7CG10b6dngxJiFtZx63VWqoTfBZ9guz3H8orI5CoH5t9acsBvNiCU1-9DaCPWrvbMJnTVWBW7L1tClMnzodqRJj1nHOL4LmpdMXYKDPx4co0CycbguC5AdyS9bb5-PnV08FBtCzSsvzJkkIoAwXyPoe6-w69JmGpU5j8HH3tjHnt2iKc9WgRcAH4V6RtPcfbj2CoDyMST-fZoLNxr8eRAzb5rmEpjnn2yYP0wmMg3h57npwwAerNYed9n11hs8zbgIZzYHeoMjU1o6Pb9HkD2G2Tb2FPpTWJ_XAXSp_VQSPXbdQP-4if-mZ-kpIdRIQ7nM1fERmDpw5jnIhEDV_n9tX-lhqUpsOJu3pCbVqtMgeOkqGsliXI8-XoUFiy3r86KHhUB2rMNsxFOKuqcESZ8THvJqrZysdPvgcpswSb0VTtgDHoUf77joZAolMUvZ0IKuD-wTmUQznsB0jQdUHGGI8WlnTVTc811-Cie1GPOpnoyqNv8EHGKR4svzI3rWoZkCIyfCcTXsRYLpQrgRNnN3t0UV4knqkmiYhogbh583hmI11XY4ZLKxW6V9nL2njwsCbFC1yf4vKp8B4HohC99V--hK5Ywp497idF6TwF8zIuQlyJZuXBvE_GfgL5bJ7B7freQRn9UcQBcPzwUN0t7Pmg8qaeYJ8jgJSDIjIvgBPwRbb4oTLKeoHOxiOL7hM83nuilCaP5K_ahO9wjC4W-l7MhX5_tgoe29HspfRlidLVv2bH3KG2kQ84CVPUQDdAS7iBmXK1unBcORTCeeACcM3iRmIRaYu-8AEmeOS0nR7XpuE_mMA-GRLuk/jhwghaHZ2AfD-FIjoMOldi8-VR8V_0yB/21)** Not as extremist lawmakers openly target Black representation. name: MAGA MELTDOWN
subject: “This is NOT supposed to be a close race!”
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY RESIST RECLAIM REBUILD PAC (WWW
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
Let me be honest with you about something.
I'm not supposed to be in this race.
The grandson of a sharecropper? Not supposed to be a viable Senate candidate in Louisiana.
A Black farmer from rural Tensas Parish? Not supposed to compete statewide in the Deep South.
Someone without billionaire backers or a Rolodex full of Washington insiders? Not supposed to have a shot at flipping a Senate seat.
But here we are.
And MAGA is absolutely shocked.
They thought Louisiana was locked up. They thought they could focus on defending seats in swing states while the South stayed safely red. They thought a race like ours — a real populist challenge to their grip on power — wasn't possible here.
They were wrong.
Look at what's happening: Democrats flipping Trump districts across the South. MAGA candidates tearing each other apart in primaries. Republican retirements at levels not seen since the Great Depression. Trump's approval cratering over his failed Iran war.
This is a once-in-a-lifetime opening. The kind of moment that doesn't come around often in Louisiana politics.
And I believe — deep in my bones — that this is the campaign to meet this moment.
Not because I'm the most polished politician. Not because I've been planning a Senate run my whole career. But because I understand what working Louisianans need because I've lived their struggles.
I know what it's like to watch costs rise while your income stays flat. I know what it's like to compete against corporations that rig the system against family operations. I know what it's like to worry about whether there will be anything left for the next generation.
That's the authentic economic populism that can win here. Not the fake MAGA version that delivers nothing but culture wars — the real thing that actually fights for working people.
And if we capitalize on this moment — if we show the political world that Louisiana is genuinely winnable — everything changes.
Not just for this race. For the entire map. For what's possible in the South.
But only if we have the resources to compete. And that counts on good folks like you stepping up.
Will you chip in $50, $25, or $10 to help us seize this once-in-a-lifetime opportunity? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
CHIP IN TO FLIP THIS SENATE SEAT! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
We have the opportunity to pull off something historic in Louisiana that will do a whole lot of good for people here. I couldn’t be more grateful to have you fighting alongside me.
Jamie Davis
Democrat for U.S. Senate

body:
Justin is still in the race for his Memphis district, fighting Tennessee Republicans' racist, gerrymandered congressional map.
#
Peter,
Justice Democrat Justin J. Pearson is standing up for voting rights and the working class in Tennessee, and he needs our support right now.
Republicans just pushed through a racist, gerrymandered congressional map designed to strip representation from Black voters in Memphis. Their goal was to make it _impossible_ for a Democrat to win this seat, which is why Justin’s incumbent opponent, Rep. Steve Cohen, has decided to retire.
**But Justin is still in this fight, and he’s going to prove them wrong.**
[](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260606-jjp.3YxLjl&refcode=em20260606-37875&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=37875%2E1203867%2E4H0Kho)
Justin refuses to back down from this fight for his community. He knows that speaking to what voters actually care about — the billionaires rigging our economy while poisoning our air and water for profit — is how you beat this Republican scheme.
Remember, this isn’t the first time Justin has stood up to the establishment and MAGA Republicans. After he was expelled from the Tennessee State House in 2023 for fighting for gun control as a member of the Tennessee Three, he commandingly won re-election — because _when you fight for people, they fight for you._
Now, it’s our turn to show up for Justin. He's not backing down, so neither can we.
**His primary election is just two months from today.** If we’re going to beat the far right and corporate interests trying to silence our working-class movement, we need to have his back.
**[Can you split $10 between Justin’s campaign and Justice Democrats now to send him to Congress to fight for us?](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260606-jjp.3YxLjl&refcode=em20260606-37875&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=3&akid=37875%2E1203867%2E4H0Kho)**
**[Contribute $10](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260606-jjp.3YxLjl&refcode=em20260606-37875&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=22&akid=37875%2E1203867%2E4H0Kho)**
In solidarity,
Justice Democrats

**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/justicedemocrats?refcode=em20260606-37875-footer&t=23&refcode2=37875_1203867_4H0Kho&akid=37875%2E1203867%2E4H0Kho)**
